evals.name: retry-ambiguity-hidden-in-happy-path
evals.prompt: Treat evals/spec-pressure-test/cases/case-001/spec.md as the complete spec available for this feature -- there is nothing else to consult. Run a spec pressure test on it.
expectations: REQUIRED: Names a concrete Blocking finding about the crash/retry window between FR-001 (local status write) and FR-002 (external webhook call) -- the spec never states which is persisted first, what happens if the process dies between them, or whether re-invoking the webhook after an indeterminate outcome is safe/idempotent.

REQUIRED: Explicitly notices that FR-004 does NOT already close this gap -- FR-004 only covers the caller re-invoking 'mark done' on an already-done task, not whether the webhook call itself may be safely re-invoked after a crash or timeout. A pass that treats FR-004 as already resolving retry safety fails this expectation.

REQUIRED: The finding includes a concrete scenario (a crash or indeterminate-outcome point between FR-001 and FR-002, or an equivalent restart/retry sequence) and names a concrete consequence (a duplicate notification to the board, or the board silently never learning the task is done, i.e. FR-003/SC-001 broken) -- not merely a general statement that 'retry behavior is unclear'.
REQUIRED: Sorts this finding as Blocking ambiguity (or the report's closest equivalent labeled bucket), not Material gap, Intentional freedom, or Already constrained.
FR-005's field-ordering freedom is either correctly noted as Intentional freedom / out of scope, or simply not raised as a problem -- it must NOT be reported as a Blocking or Material finding.

evals.name: apparent-ambiguity-already-resolved-elsewhere
evals.prompt: Treat the files in evals/spec-pressure-test/cases/case-002/ as the complete spec and its companion artifacts available for this feature -- there is nothing else to consult. Run a spec pressure test on it.
expectations: REQUIRED: Reads baseline-contract.md (not just spec.md) before drawing a conclusion about concurrent claims on a batched item.

REQUIRED: Reports the concurrent-claim question (Acceptance Scenario 3) as Already constrained, explicitly citing baseline-contract.md's claim-guarantees section (single atomic insert-if-absent, exactly one winner) as where it's resolved.

REQUIRED: Does NOT report the concurrent-claim question as a Blocking ambiguity or Material gap -- doing so, on the theory that spec.md itself is silent about it, is the specific failure this case tests for.

The report may separately note other, smaller open points about batches (e.g. duplicate item references within one batch) as Material or Intentional freedom without this affecting the pass/fail outcome, as long as the required Already-constrained finding above is present and correct.

evals.name: genuinely-permitted-implementation-divergence
evals.prompt: Treat evals/spec-pressure-test/cases/case-003/spec.md as the complete spec available for this feature -- there is nothing else to consult. Run a spec pressure test on it.
expectations: REQUIRED: Identifies that the Stale Claim Report's exact layout/column order/formatting is unspecified by FR-002 and would genuinely differ between two competent implementers.

REQUIRED: Classifies this as Intentional freedom (or the report's closest equivalent), not Blocking or Material -- and the reasoning given cites the Key Entities/Assumptions text stating the report is human-facing and nothing in scope parses its structure, rather than asserting freedom purely from the absence of a stated format.
REQUIRED: Does not report the report's exact format/layout as a Blocking or Material finding.

Does not treat the mention of piping the report through `grep` as evidence that a machine consumer depends on field order or layout -- grep does not require or benefit from a particular field order, and treating this as a reason to escalate the finding to Material or Blocking is a failure of this expectation.

evals.name: individually-reasonable-requirements-conflict-when-composed
evals.prompt: Treat evals/spec-pressure-test/cases/case-004/spec.md as the complete spec available for this feature -- there is nothing else to consult. Run a spec pressure test on it.
expectations: REQUIRED: Names a concrete contradiction between FR-001 (continuity takeover MUST be a single atomic operation, no separate release step, triggered by the acting reviewer's own real-time judgment) and the inherited baseline constraint stated in Assumptions (override release must be justified by an observed stale-claim finding, and must never be combined with a subsequent claim into one atomic operation).

REQUIRED: The finding shows both sides of the contradiction were read and connected -- referencing both FR-001's specific wording and the Assumptions bullet's specific wording, not just one of the two, or a vague sense that 'the concurrency story needs work'.

REQUIRED: Sorts this as a Blocking ambiguity (or equivalent), and explicitly frames the closing question as a choice between two options (relax FR-001's atomicity/immediate-takeover demand, or amend the inherited override-arbitration rule for this trigger condition) rather than silently picking one side as correct.
Does not resolve the contradiction by inventing an implementation detail (e.g. 'use a database lock') as if that settled which requirement wins -- the report should present the decision, not make it.

evals.name: invariant-unenforceable-at-stated-ownership-boundary
evals.prompt: Treat evals/spec-pressure-test/cases/case-005/spec.md as the complete spec available for this feature -- there is nothing else to consult. Run a spec pressure test on it.
expectations: REQUIRED: Names a concrete Blocking finding that FR-002/SC-002's absolute invariant ('never render a blocked item as available', judged against the authoritative server state at render time) cannot actually be guaranteed by a browser that FR-001/FR-003/SC-001 require to render instantly, offline-capable, from a periodically-synced local snapshot with no network call on the critical path.

REQUIRED: The finding includes a concrete scenario (an item becoming blocked shortly after the last sync, rendered before the next one) and names the resulting contradiction with FR-002/SC-002's literal wording, not just a generic comment that caches can be stale.

REQUIRED: Sorts this as Blocking ambiguity (or equivalent) and frames the closing question as a choice (weaken the invariant's wording to be relative to the last synced snapshot, or add a freshness check that would compromise the no-network-call/instant-render guarantee) rather than silently assuming one answer.

Does not treat this as merely a Material gap or a minor caching nitpick -- the fixture's SC-002 is written as an absolute guarantee, and the finding should reflect that this specific absolute wording cannot be met as the requirements are currently written.

evals.name: unreachable-or-unrecoverable-state
evals.prompt: Treat evals/spec-pressure-test/cases/case-006/spec.md as the complete spec available for this feature -- there is nothing else to consult. Run a spec pressure test on it.
expectations: REQUIRED: Notices, by walking every stated transition (FR-002, FR-003, FR-004), that no transition out of the `quarantined` status is defined anywhere in the specification.

REQUIRED: Names the concrete consequence: a quarantined file can never be deleted (no path to `deleted` exists, so FR-006/SC-002's storage-hygiene guarantee never applies to it and quarantined storage accumulates without bound) and can never be restored to `active` even after human review clears a false positive.

REQUIRED: Reports this as a Blocking ambiguity or, if reasoned explicitly as a deliberately deferred follow-up feature, a clearly-argued Material gap -- either disposition is acceptable as long as the finding itself (no exit transition from `quarantined`, with the storage/recovery consequence named) is present and concrete.

Does not describe the gap only as 'the review workflow is out of scope' without separately naming that the `quarantined` state itself has no described exit transition -- the out-of-scope review workflow is fine on its own; the missing state-machine exit is the actual finding.

evals.name: sufficiently-constrained-no-material-finding
evals.prompt: Treat evals/spec-pressure-test/cases/case-007/spec.md as the complete spec available for this feature -- there is nothing else to consult. Run a spec pressure test on it.
expectations: REQUIRED: Reaches an overall verdict of Ready to implement (or the report's closest equivalent 'no blocking issues' verdict), with no Blocking findings.

REQUIRED: Does not report a Blocking or Material finding restating retry/crash-recovery ambiguity, concurrent-recording arbitration, event-id reservation-on-rejection, or event_id uniqueness scope as unspecified -- FR-001/FR-003/FR-004, the Edge Cases section, and the Assumptions section (single-external-source scope) explicitly and correctly close all four; reporting any of them as open is a failure of this expectation regardless of how it's phrased.

The report may legitimately note, as an optional Material gap, that FR-006 doesn't specify whether the recorded-duplicate response includes the original payload/timestamp, and/or that FR-006's 'exactly three outcomes' has no home for an infrastructure failure (a DB write failure/timeout, or the signature dependency itself failing) that is neither a signature rejection nor a completed recording -- both are acceptable and do not affect pass/fail either way.

Does not pad the report with additional speculative findings (e.g. hypothetical clock skew, hypothetical malicious senders) that aren't grounded in a concrete scenario the spec's own text and scope actually support.

evals.name: concurrency-race-without-crash-or-retry
evals.prompt: Treat evals/spec-pressure-test/cases/case-008/spec.md as the complete spec available for this feature -- there is nothing else to consult. Run a spec pressure test on it.
expectations: REQUIRED: Names a concrete race between FR-001's check-then-insert (task creation checking the bundle is `open`) and FR-002's independent bundle-transition-to-review operation, with no statement of whether the two must be atomic against each other.

REQUIRED: The finding names the specific consequence -- that SC-001's absolute guarantee ('no test scenario... more tasks attached than it had at the moment it entered review') can be violated by a straightforward, literal implementation of FR-001 as a plain read-then-insert, under real concurrency -- not just a general observation that 'there might be a race'.
REQUIRED: Sorts this as Blocking ambiguity (or equivalent), given SC-001 is stated as an absolute guarantee.

Does not describe this as a retry-after-crash or failure-recovery scenario (that is a different case's failure mode) -- both operations succeed individually; the issue is pure interleaving of two independent, individually-successful operations.

evals.name: identity-uniqueness-scope-not-stated
evals.prompt: Treat evals/spec-pressure-test/cases/case-009/spec.md as the complete spec available for this feature -- there is nothing else to consult. Run a spec pressure test on it.
expectations: REQUIRED: Connects Key Entities' statement that ticket numbers are assigned 'within a given project' (i.e., only unique per project) with FR-001/FR-002's unqualified source-reference/matching format (ticket number alone, no project qualifier), and Assumptions' statement that multiple projects are routinely imported into the same tracker.

REQUIRED: Names the concrete consequence: two different tickets from two different projects sharing the same per-project ticket number would collide under FR-001's literal source-reference format, and FR-002's re-import matching would then silently overwrite an unrelated internal item's title/description with the wrong ticket's content -- not just a generic 'IDs might not be unique' comment.

REQUIRED: Sorts this as a Blocking ambiguity given the silent-data-corruption consequence, and frames the closing question as whether the source reference needs to be qualified by project (and what identifies a project stably), rather than silently assuming a project-qualified format was intended.
Explicitly connects the finding to SC-002 ('source reference always resolves back to the correct originating ticket'), which a collision directly breaks.

evals.name: ownership-authority-of-derived-status-once-set
evals.prompt: Treat evals/spec-pressure-test/cases/case-010/spec.md as the complete spec available for this feature -- there is nothing else to consult. Run a spec pressure test on it.
expectations: REQUIRED: Notices that FR-003 is only ever stated as an entry condition for moving a bundle into `review`, and that the specification never says whether a bundle's `review` status remains authoritative on its own once reached, or must continue to satisfy FR-001 OR FR-002 for as long as it stays `review`.

REQUIRED: Grounds the finding in FR-004's specific wording -- clearing the manual-ready flag 'MUST NOT affect any child task's own status' is carefully scoped to children, and conspicuously never says whether clearing it affects the bundle's own already-`review` status when computed readiness (FR-001) is also still false.

REQUIRED: Gives a concrete scenario: a bundle enters `review` only via the manual-ready flag (one child still open), the lead then clears the flag before that child finishes -- at that point neither FR-001 nor FR-002 holds, and the spec never says whether the bundle's `review` status is retroactively affected (and, if it is, there is no defined reverse transition for it to go to).

REQUIRED: Sorts this as a Blocking ambiguity, or a Material gap explicitly reasoned as such (e.g. because no stated invariant or data-integrity risk is at stake and a defensible sticky-by-default reading exists) -- either disposition is acceptable as long as the finding itself is present, concrete, and frames the choice (is `review` status an entry-gate-only fact, or an ongoing invariant tied to FR-001/FR-002) as an open question rather than silently assuming an answer.

A pass may also separately note, as a Blocking or Material finding, that FR-005's path-recording language assumes the computed and manual paths are mutually exclusive at the moment of transition when nothing prevents both being true at once -- this is not required for the case to pass, but is a legitimate, closely-related finding if raised (in either disposition, or in place of the primary finding above, as long as the entry-gate-vs-ongoing-invariant question is still substantively covered by at least one finding in the report).
